lines: Performance controller: knobs, buttons and faders are added from its menus, given labels, and mapped to as many as four parameters each anywhere in the patch
A knob, button or fader added from the module menu, sending its position to every parameter it is mapped to; right-clicking it opens its type, label, colour and mappings
Menu — Add new controller — adds a tile to the panel: a knob in Small, Medium or Large, a button in one of six kinds, or a fader in Large, X-Large or XX-Large
Menu — Add new separator — adds a Divider label for naming a section of the panel, or a Blank tile in one of six sizes
Menu — Show mapping lights on PatchMaster — lights a small indicator on each controller that has a mapping
Menu — Hide mapping indicators — takes away the coloured outline drawn around each mapped knob on the module it belongs to
Menu — Show knob arcs — draws the position arc around each knob
Menu — Show blank tiles — draws the blank separator tiles rather than leaving their space empty
Menu — Allow ctrl/cmd + click drag to move tiles — lets a tile be dragged up or down the panel with ctrl or cmd held
Menu — Precision — how often mapped parameters are written: Sample Rate, SR ÷ 4 (default), SR ÷ 128, and On changes only
Menu — Visibility (if space) — a check beside each tile's name, showing or hiding that tile where the panel has room for it
Menu — Unmap all controllers — clears every mapping on the module
Note — the knob and the button the module comes up with control nothing until they are mapped: right-click a tile, open Map 1, choose Start mapping, then click the knob it should control.
Note — right-clicking a tile opens that tile's own menu, with its name, its Controller type or Separator type, its colour, its four map slots, and Move to, Copy, Paste, Hide, Duplicate and Delete.
Note — Range, under Map 1 to Map 4 in a tile's own menu, sets the span of the mapped parameter, with Range presets of Default, Invert, 0-50%, 25-75% and 50-100%.
Note — two PatchMaster modules placed next to each other draw as one continuous panel.
Note — the module ships presets named after what they control, such as VCO, VCF, ADSR Knobs and Mixer, each laying out a set of named and labelled tiles with their mappings left empty.
Blank spacer that joins two PatchMaster modules into one continuous panel
Menu — Show vertical separator — draws a dividing line down the middle of the blank
Five-into-one signal switcher: one selected input reaches the output, and the change crossfades over about 40ms
Selects that input as the one passed to the output, silencing the other four
One of the five signals to choose between, reaching the output when its channel is selected
Carries whichever input is selected
Menu — Poly output behavior — sets the channel count of the output from the widest connected input, with Max of active inputs, or from the selected input alone, with Selected input
Menu — Top label — a box in the menu where the name printed at the top of the panel is typed
Menu — Label colour — picks the colour of that top label
Menu — Get channel names from mappings — names each channel after the parameter that the matching PatchMaster radio button controls
Five-into-one stereo signal switcher: one selected input pair reaches the outputs, and the change crossfades over about 40ms
Selects that stereo input as the one passed to the outputs, silencing the other four
The left side of one of the five stereo signals to choose between, reaching the left output when its channel is selected
The right side of one of the five stereo signals to choose between, reaching the right output when its channel is selected
Carries the left side of whichever stereo input is selected
Carries the right side of whichever stereo input is selected
Menu — Poly output behavior — sets the channel count of the output from the widest connected input, with Max of active inputs, or from the selected input alone, with Selected input
Menu — Top label — a box in the menu where the name printed at the top of the panel is typed
Menu — Label colour — picks the colour of that top label
Menu — Get channel names from mappings — names each channel after the parameter that the matching PatchMaster radio button controls
One-into-five signal switcher: the input reaches one selected output, and the change crossfades over about 40ms
Selects that output as the one the input reaches, silencing the other four
The signal routed to whichever output is selected
Carries the input while its channel is selected, and silence otherwise
Menu — Top label — a box in the menu where the name printed at the top of the panel is typed
Menu — Label colour — picks the colour of that top label
Menu — Get channel names from mappings — names each channel after the parameter that the matching PatchMaster radio button controls
One-into-five stereo signal switcher: the input pair reaches one selected output pair, and the change crossfades over about 40ms
Selects that output pair as the one the input reaches, silencing the other four
The left signal routed to whichever output is selected
The right signal routed to whichever output is selected
Carries the left input while its channel is selected, and silence otherwise
Carries the right input while its channel is selected, and silence otherwise
Menu — Top label — a box in the menu where the name printed at the top of the panel is typed
Menu — Label colour — picks the colour of that top label
Menu — Get channel names from mappings — names each channel after the parameter that the matching PatchMaster radio button controls
Master output strip with fader, RMS and peak VU, mute with fade automation, dim, mono fold, soft clipping and a DC blocker
Sets the output level, -inf to +6dB with unity at 0dB; the VU is calibrated so that 0dB reads 10V
Mutes the output, and becomes a fade button once fade automation is turned on in the label menu
Drops the output by the amount set as the dim gain in the label menu, -12dB by default
Folds the output to mono
Left input into the strip
Right input into the strip
Left output, after the fader, dim, mono fold, DC blocker and clipper
Right output, after the fader, dim, mono fold, DC blocker and clipper
Menu — Symmetrical fades — makes a fade-in and a fade-out follow mirrored curves
Menu — Fade — two sliders, the first setting the fade time from OFF to 30 seconds, the second the curve, Linear at the centre with Exp and Log either side
Menu — Dim gain — sets how far the DIM button drops the output, -30dB to -1dB, and -12dB by default
Menu — DC blocker — passes only the AC part of the output
Menu — Clipping — Soft (default), which starts at -4.44dB and reaches its limit at +1.58dB, or Hard, which holds the output to 10V
Menu — VU Colour — sets the colour of the meter
Menu — Display colour — sets the colour of the label
Note — the fade time, the fade curve and the dim gain are on the module's own right-click menu, along with the box the label is typed into.
Four-band parametric EQ for all 24 tracks, groups and aux busses of a MixMaster, patched in through the mixer's polyphonic inserts, with one set of band controls showing the track that is selected
Selects which of the 24 tracks the band controls, the gain, the spectrum display and the meter belong to
Switches the EQ of the selected track between active and bypassed
Bypasses the EQ on all 24 tracks at once
Sets the output gain of the selected track, -20dB to +20dB
Switches that band in or out of the selected track's EQ
Switches the low band between a low shelf and a bell
Switches the high band between a high shelf and a bell
Sets the frequency of the low band, 20Hz to 500Hz
Sets the frequency of the low-mid band, 30Hz to 2kHz
Sets the frequency of the high-mid band, 500Hz to 5kHz
Sets the frequency of the high band, 1kHz to 20kHz
Sets the boost or cut of that band, -20dB to +20dB
Sets the Q of that band, 0.3 to 20, narrowing it as the value rises
Takes the mixer's poly insert send for tracks 1 to 8, sixteen channels carrying a left and a right for each
Takes the mixer's poly insert send for tracks 9 to 16, sixteen channels carrying a left and a right for each
Takes the mixer's poly insert send for the four group busses and four aux busses, sixteen channels carrying a left and a right for each
Carries tracks 1 to 8 back to the mixer's poly insert return
Carries tracks 9 to 16 back to the mixer's poly insert return
Carries the four group busses and four aux busses back to the mixer's poly insert return
Menu — Link to mixer — takes the 24 track names and colours from a named MixMaster in the patch
Menu — Track/band active CVs — reads the EqSpander jacks as Trigger toggle, or as Gate high/low
Menu — Analyser decay — sets how fast the spectrum display falls back
Menu — Hide EQ curves when bypassed — stops a bypassed track's curve being drawn in the display
Menu — Knob arcs — draws the knob position arc, the CV arc, both or neither
Menu — Display colour — sets the colour of the readouts
Menu — VU colour — sets the colour of the meter
Note — the EQ does nothing until a poly insert cable from a MixMaster is patched into one of the three inputs and the matching output is patched back to the mixer.
Note — right-clicking the track label opens a menu of its own, with Initialize track settings, Copy track settings to:, Move track settings to: and a Select Track list of all 24.
Note — right-clicking a band's frequency readout opens a menu of its own, with that band's CV attenuator and a Show freq as note item that reads the frequencies out as note names.
Note — right-clicking a knob types an exact value into it.
CV expander for EqMaster, placed on either side of it, with polyphonic CV over the band controls and the active state of all 24 tracks
Sixteen channels of CV for that track's EQ, four channels per band running from low to high, each band taking active, then frequency, then gain, then Q
Switches the EQ of tracks 1 to 16 in and out, one track per channel
Switches the EQ of the four groups in and out on channels 1 to 4 and the four auxes on channels 5 to 8, with the global bypass on channel 9
Note — the expander does nothing on its own: it must be placed immediately beside an EqMaster, on either side of it, and the jacks then drive that EqMaster.
Poly merge for the MixMaster inserts and CV inputs: the poly input is normalled to the poly output, and each mono input replaces its channel there or adds to it when that channel is unused
The sixteen-channel signal normalled to the poly output
Carries the poly input with the patched mono inputs merged into their channels
Replaces the left channel of that track in the poly output, or adds to it when that poly channel carries nothing
Replaces the right channel of that track in the poly output, or adds to it when that poly channel carries nothing
Green passes that track's pair of mono inputs to the poly output, red drops them so that the poly input's own two channels pass instead
Menu — Audio panels — relabels the jacks for tracks 1-8, tracks 9-16 or the group and aux busses
Menu — CV panels — relabels the jacks for the MixMaster and AuxSpander poly CV inputs: mute, solo, group and master mute and solo, the four aux sends, the send mutes and the aux bus jacks
Menu — CV panels Jr — relabels the jacks for the MixMasterJr and AuxSpanderJr poly CV inputs
Note — the panel choice only relabels the jacks; it changes nothing about what the module does with them.
Meld.notes: No port family is given: the panel can be switched between audio and CV labels, so what a jack carries depends on what is patched.

lines: Poly split for the MixMaster inserts and direct outs, breaking a sixteen-channel cable into eight stereo pairs of mono outputs, with a thru output carrying the poly signal onward
The sixteen-channel signal split across the mono outputs
Carries a copy of the poly input
Carries the left channel of that track from the poly input
Carries the right channel of that track from the poly input
Menu — Panel — relabels the jacks for tracks 1-8, tracks 9-16 or the group and aux busses
Note — the panel choice only relabels the jacks; it changes nothing about what the module does with them.
Unmeld.notes: No port family is given: the module carries whatever poly cable is patched into it.

lines: Routing utility that spreads a MixMaster insert cable into separate left and right cables, so that VCV Mid/Side and EqMaster can process the mid and side of eight tracks at a time
Takes the mixer's poly insert send for those eight tracks, sixteen channels carrying a left and a right for each
Carries the left channel of each of those eight tracks, placed on channels 1, 3, 5 and so on with the channels between them silent
Carries the right channel of each of those eight tracks, placed on channels 1, 3, 5 and so on with the channels between them silent
Takes the processed left channels of those eight tracks back, reading channels 1, 3, 5 and so on
Takes the processed right channels of those eight tracks back, reading channels 1, 3, 5 and so on
Carries the left and right returns interleaved into one sixteen-channel cable for the mixer's poly insert return
Dual band stereo width processor: the input is split at a crossover frequency and the stereo width and level of the low and high bands are set separately
Sets the frequency at which the input splits into a low band and a high band, 50Hz to 500Hz
Sets the crossover slope to 12dB per octave or 24dB per octave
Sets the stereo width of the low band, 0% collapsing it to mono, 100% leaving it as it came in and 200% doubling it
Sets the stereo width of the high band, 0% collapsing it to mono, 100% leaving it as it came in and 200% doubling it
Silences the high band so that only the low band reaches the output, and switching it on clears the high band solo
Silences the low band so that only the high band reaches the output, and switching it on clears the low band solo
Sets the level of the low band, -20dB to +20dB
Sets the level of the high band, -20dB to +20dB
Passes the input to the output unprocessed
Left input
Right input
Left output
Right output
Menu — Crossover slope — 12 db/oct or 24 db/oct
Menu — Poly input behavior — Sum each input (L, R) adds the channels of each poly input on its own, Sum to stereo (L only) reads one poly cable in the left input as a stereo mix
Menu — Display colour — picks the colour of the value readouts
BassMasterJr.notes: Params 9 and 10, master gain and mix, exist on this model but have no control on the panel and no effect on the sound; they are drawn and used on BassMaster.

Crossfades the output between the untouched input at 0% and the fully processed signal at 100%

Adds to the high band width setting, each volt shifting it by 20 percentage points

Menu — VU scaling — Scale as track calibrates the meter so 0dB is 5V, Scale as master so 0dB is 10V
Menu — VU colour — picks the colour of the meter
Eight-channel multi-stage envelope generator and complex LFO: each channel plays a shape you draw, with its own VCA, CV output, trigger modes, crossover and sidechain trigger detection
Sets the cycle length of that channel, 0.56ms to 30 minutes; right-clicking it takes a length typed in seconds
Sets how many times the shape cycles once it starts playing, 1 to 99, or endlessly at the INF setting
Holds the shape back by as many as 8192 samples after a trigger arrives, in Trigger and Sidechain modes
Runs alternate cycles fast and the ones between them slow, -99% to +99%
Shifts the shape through its cycle, 0 to 360 degrees
Stretches or compresses the shape vertically along an exponential curve, -100% to +100%
Stretches the shape horizontally towards one end of the cycle and compresses it at the other, -100% to +100%
Attenuates the output voltage, 0 to 100%
Limits how fast the output voltage can change, measured against the cycle length so that 50% turns a square wave into a triangle
Filters the output voltage to soften the clicks that steep vertical changes in the shape make, 0 to 100%
Splits the audio through the VCA into a low band and a high band at this frequency, 20Hz to 20kHz, and turns the crossover off at its lowest setting
Attenuates how far the shape modulates the high band of the VCA, 0 to 100%
Attenuates how far the shape modulates the low band of the VCA, 0 to 100%

Starts the playhead on that channel, and pressing it during play stops the playhead and resets it; alt-clicking resets the channel
Holds the playhead in place, with the voltage under it held at the CV output

Audio into that channel's VCA, whose gain the shape modulates over 0-10V whatever the CV range is set to

That channel's VCA input with the shape applied to its amplitude

Menu — Run off setting — stops and resets every channel when run goes off, or freezes them where they are
Menu — Show channel labels — draws each channel's name in the graph window
Menu — Show node tooltip — reads out the voltage and the time of a node while the pointer is over it
Menu — Show shape nodes — hides the nodes and the curve control points until one is under the pointer
Menu — Line width — a slider setting the thickness of the shape, 0.3pt to 2pt
Menu — Shadow — picks which side of the shape the shaded area is drawn on
Menu — Knob label display colour — sets the colour of the readouts under the knobs
Menu — Knob arcs — draws the knob position arc, the CV arc, both or neither
Menu — Cloaked mode — turns off the drawing that is not needed, to save processor time
Note — a channel plays only while run is on and that channel's play button is on; in Trigger, Gate or Sidechain mode it starts only when something arrives at its TRIG input.
Note — double-clicking in the graph window adds a node and double-clicking a node deletes it; shift-dragging draws a stepped pattern, and alt or ctrl dragging snaps a node to the grid.
Note — right-clicking in the graph window opens a menu of its own carrying Add node, and right-clicking a node opens one with that node's time and voltage and a Delete node item.
Note — right-clicking a channel button opens that channel's own menu, with its label and colour, gain adjust at the VCA input, poly VCA summing, retrigger, and copy, paste and initialise.

ShapeMaster.notes: Input 16, the clock input, has no jack on this free version's panel and is left untagged; clock sync is a ShapeMaster Pro feature. The two length params, sync and unsync, share one knob position, so both are tagged to the length line.

lines: 8-track stereo mixer with two group busses, polyphonic inserts and direct outs on every track and bus, filters and fade automation per track, and CV over volume, pan, mute and solo
Left input of that track, and the whole of it for a mono track; a polyphonic cable patched here is summed to one signal
Right input of that track, making it stereo; a polyphonic cable patched here is summed to one signal
Sets the level of that track over 0-10V, scaled so that 10V gives the level its fader is set to
Pans that track over -5V to 5V, added to its pan knob and attenuated by the pan CV input level in its track menu
Pans that track across the stereo field, following the mono pan law and stereo pan mode set in the global menu
Sets the level of that track, -inf to +6dB with unity at 0dB; ctrl-clicking or cmd-clicking adds it to the group of linked faders
Mutes that track, and becomes a fade button once fade automation is turned on in its track menu
Solos that track, and more than one track can be soloed at a time
Routes that track to one of the group busses, or to the master bus when it reads as a dash
Sets the high pass filter on that track, 20Hz to 1kHz at 18dB per octave, and off below 20Hz
Sets the low pass filter on that track, 20kHz down to 1kHz at 12dB per octave, and off above 20kHz
Sets the level of that group bus over 0-10V, scaled so that 10V gives the level its fader is set to
Pans that group bus over -5V to 5V, added to its pan knob and attenuated by the pan CV input level in its bus menu
Pans that group bus across the stereo field, following the stereo pan mode set in the global menu
Sets the level of that group bus, -inf to +6dB with unity at 0dB; ctrl-clicking or cmd-clicking adds it to the group of linked faders
Mutes that group bus, and becomes a fade button once fade automation is turned on in its bus menu
Solos that group bus, and the tracks routed into it play unless one of them is soloed on its own
Sets the high pass filter on that group bus, 20Hz to 1kHz at 18dB per octave, and off below 20Hz
Sets the low pass filter on that group bus, 20kHz down to 1kHz at 12dB per octave, and off above 20kHz
Sets the level of the main output, -inf to +6dB with unity at 0dB; the master VU is calibrated so that 0dB reads 10V
Mutes the main output, and becomes a fade button once fade automation is turned on in the master menu
Drops the main output by the amount set as the dim gain in the master menu, -12dB by default
Folds the main output to mono
Left side of a stereo signal mixed into the main output, before the master fader or after it as the global menu is set
Right side of a stereo signal mixed into the main output, before the master fader or after it as the global menu is set
Left main output, carrying the whole mix after the master fader, the clipper and the DC blocker
Right main output, carrying the whole mix after the master fader, the clipper and the DC blocker
Sends tracks 1 to 8 out of the signal path as sixteen channels, each track on a left and a right channel
Sends the busses out of the signal path as sixteen channels: the two groups on channels 1 to 4 and the four aux returns on channels 9 to 16
Returns tracks 1 to 8 to the signal path, and every one of the eight tracks has to come back on this cable or it falls silent in the mixer
Returns the two group busses and four aux busses to the signal path, and every bus sent out has to come back on this cable or it falls silent in the mixer
Carries tracks 1 to 8 as sixteen channels tapped at the point chosen in the global menu, each track on a left and a right channel
Carries the busses as sixteen channels: the two group busses on channels 1 to 4 and the four aux busses on channels 9 to 16
Carries the fade level of each track as eight channels of 0-10V, one channel per track
Mutes tracks 1 to 8 from channels 1 to 8 and solos them from channels 9 to 16, reading a trigger that toggles or a gate as the global menu is set, not the packing the manual shows
Mutes the two group busses on channels 1 and 2, solos them on channels 3 and 4, and takes master mute on channel 5, dim on 6, mono on 7 and volume on 8, not the packing the manual shows
Menu — Direct outs — picks the tap point for the direct out jacks: pre-insert, post-insert, post-fader or post mute-solo, or set per track
Menu — Chain input — mixes the chain jacks in before the master fader or after it
Menu — Mono pan law — sets the boost given to a mono signal as it is panned: 0dB, +3dB, +4.5dB or +6dB
Menu — Stereo pan mode — chooses linear stereo balance, equal power stereo balance or true panning, globally or per track
Menu — Filters — places the high and low pass filters before the inserts or after them
Menu — Mute/Solo CV — reads the mute and solo CV jacks as a rising edge that toggles, or as a gate that is high at 10V
Menu — Vol CV inputs — scale the fader in the same curve the fader itself uses, or linearly
Menu — Fades — turns on symmetrical fade curves, and adds the volume CV into the fade CV output
Menu — Knob arcs — draws both the knob position arc and the CV arc, the CV arc alone, or neither
Menu — Fader CV pointers — draws a pointer on each fader showing where its volume CV has put it
Menu — VU colour — sets the meter colour for the whole mixer or per track
Menu — Display colour — sets the label colour for the whole mixer or per track
Menu — Cloaked mode — turns off every VU except the master one, saving processor time
Menu — Eco mode — samples the faders, the pan knobs and their CV inputs at a quarter of the audio rate
Menu — Poly-spread V and P track 1 — sends channel N of a poly cable in track 1's V or P jack to track N
Menu — Copy mixer — under MixMaster swap, takes every setting of this mixer, to be pasted into another of the same size
Menu — Paste mixer — under MixMaster swap, writes the settings copied from another mixer of the same size onto this one
Menu — MixMaster swap — a submenu holding Copy mixer and Paste mixer, which move a whole mixer's settings to another MixMaster
Note — right-clicking a track label opens that track's own menu, with gain adjustment, the two filters, the pan CV attenuator, fade time and curve, fader linking, and copy and move actions.
Note — right-clicking the master label opens the master's own menu, with the fade time and curve, the dim gain and the clipping choice.
Note — the track VUs read 0dB at 5V and clip at +6dB, while the master VU reads 0dB at 10V; a master channel that clips turns its whole meter red.
Note — the Aux sends, Aux returns and Routing returns to groups items appear on this menu only while an AuxSpander is placed immediately to the right.
MixMasterJr.notes: The shipped manual documents the 16-track layout only, and this model packs its CV jacks differently, so the two CV lines each carry a clause saying so. The 16-track mixer has one poly jack for track mutes and another for track solos; here a single jack takes mutes on channels 1 to 8 and solos on channels 9 to 16. Its group and master jack takes group mutes on channels 1 and 2, group solos on 3 and 4, master mute on 5, dim on 6, mono on 7 and master volume on 8, where the 16-track version uses channels 1 to 4, 5 to 8, and 9 to 12 for the master controls.

lines: Four aux send and return busses for MixMasterJr, placed immediately to the right of it, with a send level per track and per group, filters and panning on each return, and CV over nearly all of it

Sets how much of that group bus goes to that aux bus, -inf to 0dB, taken from the point in the group's signal path chosen in the mixer's aux sends menu
Mutes all four aux sends for that track, leaving only its dry signal in the mix
Mutes all four aux sends for that group bus, leaving only its dry signal in the mix
Sets the level of everything feeding that aux bus's send jacks, -inf to +12dB with unity at 0dB
Pans that aux return across the stereo field, following the stereo pan mode set in the mixer's global menu
Sets the level of that aux return into the mix, -inf to +6dB with unity at 0dB
Mutes that aux return, and becomes a fade button once fade automation is turned on in its bus menu
Solos that aux return, which silences the other three returns and leaves the mixer's own tracks playing
Routes that aux return to one of the group busses, or to the master bus when it reads as a dash
Left send from that aux bus to its effect
Right send from that aux bus to its effect
Left return from that aux bus's effect, and patched on its own it feeds both sides of the return
Right return from that aux bus's effect
Sets the aux A send levels of tracks 1 to 8 from channels 1 to 8 and the aux B levels of those tracks from channels 9 to 16, each -10V to 10V added to the knob, not the packing the manual shows
Sets the aux C send levels of tracks 1 to 8 from channels 1 to 8 and the aux D levels of those tracks from channels 9 to 16, each -10V to 10V added to the knob, not the packing the manual shows
Mutes the aux sends of tracks 1 to 8 from channels 1 to 8 and of the two group busses from channels 9 and 10, reading a rising edge that toggles or a gate, not the packing the manual shows
Sets the group bus aux send levels from -10V to 10V added to the knobs, the two groups on channels 1 and 2 for aux A, 3 and 4 for B, 5 and 6 for C and 7 and 8 for D, not the packing the manual shows
Sets the four global send levels from -5V to 5V on channels 1 to 4, the four return pans the same way on channels 5 to 8, and the four return levels from 0-10V on channels 9 to 12
Mutes the four aux returns from channels 1 to 4 and solos them from channels 5 to 8, reading a rising edge that toggles or a gate
Menu — Aux sends — on the mixer's own menu rather than this one, picks the tap point for every send: pre-insert, post-insert, post-fader or post mute-solo
Menu — Aux sends — also carries a setting that mutes a track's sends whenever its group is muted
Menu — Aux returns — on the mixer's own menu rather than this one, can mute the returns when a track is soloed, and mute the tracks when a return is soloed
Menu — Routing returns to groups — on the mixer's own menu rather than this one, switches off the protection that silences the aux send of a group a return is routed into
Note — the expander does nothing on its own: it must be placed immediately to the right of a MixMasterJr, which is the mixer whose sends and returns it carries.

AuxExpanderJr.notes: The shipped manual documents the 16-track layout only, and this model packs its CV jacks differently, so the four affected lines each carry a clause saying so. On the 16-track expander one poly jack carries one aux send's levels for all sixteen tracks; here each jack carries two auxes for eight tracks, aux A on channels 1 to 8 and aux B on 9 to 16, then aux C and aux D the same way. The 16-track expander mutes track sends on one jack and group sends on another; here one jack takes the eight tracks on channels 1 to 8 and the two groups on channels 9 and 10. The group send level jack packs two groups per aux, on channels 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, and 7 and 8, where the 16-track version uses four channels per aux.

Right main output, carrying the whole mix after the master fader, the clipper and the DC blocker

Menu — Direct outs — picks the tap point for the direct out jacks: pre-insert, post-insert, post-fader or post mute-solo, or set per track
Menu — Chain input — mixes the chain jacks in before the master fader or after it
Menu — Mono pan law — sets the boost given to a mono signal as it is panned: 0dB, +3dB, +4.5dB or +6dB
Menu — Stereo pan mode — chooses linear stereo balance, equal power stereo balance or true panning, globally or per track
Menu — Filters — places the high and low pass filters before the inserts or after them
Menu — Mute/Solo CV — reads the mute and solo CV jacks as a rising edge that toggles, or as a gate that is high at 10V
Menu — Vol CV inputs — scale the fader in the same curve the fader itself uses, or linearly
Menu — Fades — turns on symmetrical fade curves, and adds the volume CV into the fade CV output
Menu — Knob arcs — draws both the knob position arc and the CV arc, the CV arc alone, or neither
Menu — Fader CV pointers — draws a pointer on each fader showing where its volume CV has put it
Menu — VU colour — sets the meter colour for the whole mixer or per track
Menu — Display colour — sets the label colour for the whole mixer or per track
Menu — Cloaked mode — turns off every VU except the master one, saving processor time
Menu — Eco mode — samples the faders, the pan knobs and their CV inputs at a quarter of the audio rate
Menu — Poly-spread V and P track 1 — sends channel N of a poly cable in track 1's V or P jack to track N
Menu — Copy mixer — under MixMaster swap, takes every setting of this mixer, to be pasted into another of the same size
Menu — Paste mixer — under MixMaster swap, writes the settings copied from another mixer of the same size onto this one
Menu — MixMaster swap — a submenu holding Copy mixer and Paste mixer, which move a whole mixer's settings to another MixMaster
Note — right-clicking a track label opens that track's own menu, with gain adjustment, the two filters, the pan CV attenuator, fade time and curve, fader linking, and copy and move actions.
Note — right-clicking the master label opens the master's own menu, with the fade time and curve, the dim gain and the clipping choice.
Note — the track VUs read 0dB at 5V and clip at +6dB, while the master VU reads 0dB at 10V; a master channel that clips turns its whole meter red.
Note — the Aux sends, Aux returns and Routing returns to groups items appear on this menu only while an AuxSpander is placed immediately to the right.

Sets how much of that group bus goes to that aux bus, -inf to 0dB, taken from the point in the group's signal path chosen in the mixer's aux sends menu

Mutes all four aux sends for that group bus, leaving only its dry signal in the mix

Mutes that aux return, and becomes a fade button once fade automation is turned on in its bus menu

Left send from that aux bus to its effect
Right send from that aux bus to its effect
Left return from that aux bus's effect, and patched on its own it feeds both sides of the return
Right return from that aux bus's effect
Sets the send levels of tracks 1 to 16 into that aux bus, one track per channel, each -10V to 10V added to the track's send knob
Mutes the aux sends of tracks 1 to 16, one track per channel, reading a rising edge that toggles or a gate
Sets the group bus aux send levels from -10V to 10V added to the knobs, the four groups taking channels 1 to 4 for aux A, 5 to 8 for aux B, 9 to 12 for aux C and 13 to 16 for aux D
Mutes the aux sends of the four group busses on channels 1 to 4, reading a rising edge that toggles or a gate
Sets the four global send levels from -5V to 5V on channels 1 to 4, the four return pans the same way on channels 5 to 8, and the four return levels from 0-10V on channels 9 to 12

Menu — Aux sends — on the mixer's own menu rather than this one, picks the tap point for every send: pre-insert, post-insert, post-fader or post mute-solo
Menu — Aux sends — also carries a setting that mutes a track's sends whenever its group is muted
Menu — Aux returns — on the mixer's own menu rather than this one, can mute the returns when a track is soloed, and mute the tracks when a return is soloed
Menu — Routing returns to groups — on the mixer's own menu rather than this one, switches off the protection that silences the aux send of a group a return is routed into
Note — the expander does nothing on its own: it must be placed immediately to the right of a MixMaster, which is the mixer whose sends and returns it carries.
